terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A parked vehicle prop: an exterior shell with no interior geometry, since a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside and the glazing is authored as a tinted, mostly opaque pane. The wheels are the mechanisms: each is a named pivot on its axle. Nothing else moves and nothing attaches, so there are no sockets. The most common vehicle on Thai roads. The plate shows a navy underbone with white pinstripes on the leg shield and side covers, a black vinyl seat, a chrome rear rack with a slotted plate, round chrome mirrors on tall stems, a rectangular headlamp between amber indicators, silver engine cases with a near-horizontal barrel under the frame spine, a chain to a rear sprocket, a dusty exhaust on the right and wire-spoked wheels with drum hubs.

reasoning: The identity is the underbone layout: a leg shield rising to a handlebar cowl, a step-through floor, side covers under a flat seat, a chrome rack behind it, wire-spoked wheels front and rear. It is an assembly of small parts, not one shell.

Three materials: the paint (leg shield, fork cover, frame spine, covers, seat, fenders, cowl, swingarm, pinstripes as vertex colours), a white vertex-coloured trim carrying chrome, alloy, lamps and black rubber, and a third for the tyres, whose tread tile has to multiply the rubber without touching anything else.
One repetition system: two wheels off one open wire-wheel geometry, each a named pivot on its axle.
Action readiness is the wheels: two hinge pivots, convex collider, not breakable. Steering is not articulated.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A motorcycle is legible by its silhouette gaps as much as its masses -- the step-through, the daylight under the seat, the space inside the fork, and above all the daylight THROUGH a wire wheel -- so the frame is tubes, the panels are thin extrusions, and the wheel is an open tyre ring with a rim, a drum hub and twenty-six prism spokes rather than a dished disc.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The wheels are wire-spoked in the plate and are built OPEN: a closed tyre-ring lathe, a rim ring, a drum hub and twenty-six three-sided prism spokes, with daylight through them. The first build used the closed dished lathe, which is a solid disc that HIDES the spokes merged into it -- it shipped two grey discs.

The turntable gate's enclosed-background signal fires on the step-through gap, the daylight inside the fork, under the seat and now through the wire wheels: real open air on a motorcycle. --allow-holes is set on the _holecc measurement.
The right side is mirrored from the left; the exhaust runs on the right, dull and dusty rather than bright chrome (measured #4d4137 on the plate's silencer).
The chain, sprockets and kickstart are read off the plate's left-side crop; the countershaft sprocket is inferred behind its cover at confidence 0.75.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.71 x 1.25 x 1.92 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=8 draw calls, <=4 materials, <=8 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus one named pivot per wheel (2); zero sockets; convex collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

silhouette.description: Wheels 0.556 m in diameter at z +0.64 and -0.58 (1.22 wheelbase); a front fender hugging the tyre at 18-38 mm from 4 to 134 degrees; chrome fork sliders on 27 degrees of rake THROUGH the front hub, under a 0.19 m navy FORK COVER on the fork line from 0.60 to 0.845 m and a triple clamp at 0.83; a handlebar cowl 0.87-1.015 m carrying a rectangular headlamp and two amber pods, its top edges filleted at 45 mm; bars at 1.00 m across 0.69 m with mirrors to 1.258 m; a leg shield from 0.30 to 0.87 m, front face z +0.575, top edge back at z +0.30, its outer front edges wrapped back on an 85 mm plan radius; a step-through floor at 0.28-0.32 m with a navy frame SPINE rising from it (z +0.46, y 0.31-0.45) to the seat nose (z +0.14, y 0.69); side covers 0.47-0.672 m from z +0.08 to -0.47 under a seat at 0.674-0.760 m from z +0.11 to -0.46 with 45 mm shoulders and 60 mm end roundings; a chrome rack at 0.70 m over z -0.46..-0.93; engine 0.19-0.40 m between the wheels with the barrel laid 74 degrees forward under the spine. Band table against the proxy (scratch/_mon/bands.mjs): mean |dw| 0.021 H, mean |dd| 0.052 H; the one residual over 0.1 is band 2 (+0.125 H), the front fender lip and the rear mudflap at hub height, both of which the plate shows and the proxy fused away.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -0.356..+0.356 at the mirror heads; y 0.000 to 1.258 at the mirror tips; z -0.939 to +0.942, rear mudflap to front fender, +Z forward. The Meshy proxy (bbox 1.897 x 1.240 x 0.727) normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.654 : 0.383, i.e. 1.92 x 1.255 x 0.735 at the declared length, and the wheel centres sit at 0.15 L and 0.80 L for a 1.23 m wheelbase. The registry height of 1.07 was a list-time estimate to the BAR TOPS; it has been corrected to 1.25 on the proxy arithmetic, with the bars still at 1.00 and the mirrors carrying the rest.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.654 : 0.383. Its side elevation and occupancy map (scratch/honda-wave/_ev/) read wheel centres at 0.15 L and 0.80 L, bars at 0.80 H, mirror tips at 0.98 H, seat top at 0.60 H over 0.50-0.73 L, rack at 0.545 H = 0.68 m over 0.75-0.98 L and the leg shield spanning 0.21-0.35 L -- and those fractions at the declared 1.92 m are what is built. The first build read the same map at a wrong length and put the front axle 0.12 m too far back.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.80: the plate shows the left side; the right is mirrored, with the exhaust on the right as the type has it.

componentTree.name: Bodywork: leg shield, covers, fenders, cowl and seat
componentTree.topologyRationale: Eight thin side-profile extrusions (leg shield with 28 percent tumblehome and wrapped front edges, a fork cover on the fork line, a frame spine flooring the step-through, side covers, seat pad with filleted shoulders, two fenders hugging their tyres, handlebar cowl), the floor cover, seven pinstripe boxes and five painted tube runs (swingarm, shock bodies) merged into ONE geometry and ONE draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Leg shield 0.30-0.87 m over z +0.30..+0.575, 0.36 wide; fork cover 0.60-0.845 m on the fork line, 0.19 wide tapering 22 percent; spine z +0.46..+0.02, 0.31-0.70 m, 0.15 wide; covers 0.47-0.672 m from z +0.08 to -0.47, 0.225 wide; seat 0.674-0.760 m from z +0.11 to -0.46, 0.285 wide so it overhangs the covers; front fender 4..134 deg at 18-38 mm off the tread; cowl 0.87-1.015 m.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Every panel is a separate thin extrusion at its own width; the fork cover (0.19) and spine (0.15) sit inside the 0.36 shield and under the 0.285 seat with no shared plane; the seat is 0.285 wide over 0.225-wide covers and meets them as an opposed butt; the fenders stand 18 mm off the tread; pinstripes stand 4 mm proud of the tumbled flank. check-coplanar reports clean at 0.001 m.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with height-keyed UVs for the dust tile.

textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

evidence: WHITE with vertexColors under a tread canvas bound AFTER construction: the tyre carries #6e675d, the rim #a9a7a2, the drum hub #8a8378 and the spokes #b0aea9. Measured tread #49453e on region-tyre (0.841), authored 1.275x against the tile's base of 200/255 so dust and scuffs can go brighter than the rubber under a multiply canvas, and lifted to luma 105 so the back-lit 180 frame (0.55 of painted luma) clears the gate's 58.

Its UVs are around-by-profile at 0.05 m per repeat (35 repeats on a 0.556 m wheel); the rim, hub and spokes pin to the tile's white top 4% so their vertex colours render unmultiplied. It is its own material because a tread that multiplied the chrome and the paint would ruin both.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components and one repetition system: 3 of 8. Sixty-odd fittings ride one merge.

materials.note: paint, a white vertex-coloured trim and a rubber carrying the tread tile: 3 of 4. Chrome, alloy, vinyl and lamps differ in albedo only and share the trim; the tyre is separate ONLY because its canvas would otherwise multiply them.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,716 of 4,000: the open wire wheel is the cost at ~600 triangles per geometry (two instances), and every tube run whose ends are buried is built open, which is half the triangles of a capped one.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Thin side-profile extrusions for the panels and the tyre-hugging fenders, polyline tubes for the frame, drivetrain and fittings, lathes for the lamp pods and engine covers, an open wire-wheel lathe, boxes for the rest.
One InstancedMesh carries both wheels. No per-instance colour.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Every material is declared textureless. Two canvases are bound after construction: a 256 px dust multiplier on the paint and a 256 px tread on the rubber. 0.7 MB of texture VRAM, factory 85 ms.

risks.description: The turntable gate flags the step-through, the fork daylight and now the gaps between the spokes.
risks.mitigation: Real open air on a motorcycle; --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement logged per azimuth.

risks.description: The right side is not in the plate.
3,976 of 4,000 leaves under 1 percent of headroom; nothing more fits without taking something out.
risks.mitigation: Wheel seg 16 and 26 spokes are the levers; thin chrome runs are already six-sided and 22 tube runs open.
